title: Starting trombone with Jim Humphrey, 1919
summary: He took up music at about 17; a cousin gave him a violin but Humphrey steered him to trombone.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: I have brothers, but none of them didn't take up no music. And I didn't take up music until around 1919. At that time I was around 17, 17 years old. And I started on the trombone. The trombone. And I was taking lessons from Professor J.B. Humphrey. Oh yes. Jim Humphrey. Jim Humphrey.
I was going to ask you about your first instrument. Did you happen to have a trombone around? How did you happen to settle on that instrument? Did your...

Well, I tell you, I had a cousin. He was a client at Flair. And he's the one who urged me to start music. Well, he had an old violin. He gave it to me. So I went to old man Hoffrey. And he told me, he said, you're wasting your time fooling around with an instrument like this. He said, because this instrument is not dying out. It's done dying out. So he advised me to take up the trombone. So that's why you settled on that. That's why I settled on the trombone.
